title: Derived change of rings along a morphism of sheaves of rings, computed by K-flat resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$; let $D(\mathcal O)$, $D(\mathcal O')$ be the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian categories of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules and of $\mathcal O'$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a complex $\mathcal P^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules write $\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ for the complex of $\mathcal O'$-modules obtained by applying the change of rings $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] termwise. Then: (1) if $\alpha:\mathcal P^\bullet\to\mathcal Q^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] between K-flat complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex], the induced map $\alpha\otimes1:\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'\to\mathcal Q^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal O'$-modules; (2) consequently there is an exact functor of triangulated categories $L\varphi^*=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O':D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$, the left derived functor of the termwise change of rings $K(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$, $\mathcal G^\bullet\mapsto\mathcal G^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$, which is everywhere defined and computed by K-flat complexes: for every K-flat resolution $\mathcal P^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] the canonical map $L\varphi^*\mathcal G^\bullet\to\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ (inverse of the map induced by the resolution) is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O')$, and for two K-flat resolutions $\mathcal P^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$, $\mathcal P'^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ the resulting isomorphism $\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'\cong\mathcal P'^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ in $D(\mathcal O')$ is canonical (compatible with composition for a third resolution).

source.place: Section 'Flat resolutions' (Tag 06YL): Lemma Tag 06YT (sites-cohomology-lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side) with $\mathcal F^\bullet=\mathcal O'$ in degree 0 for (1), and the construction before Definition Tag 06YU; Section 'Derived pullback' (Tag 06YV): Lemma Tag 06YY (sites-cohomology-lemma-derived-base-change) for the morphism of ringed topoi $(\Sh(\mathcal C),\mathcal O')\to(\Sh(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)$ given by the identity of $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ and $\varphi$, whose pullback $f^*$ is $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$, using literature/stacks-project/derived.tex, Lemma Tag 06XN (derived-lemma-find-existence-computes) for (2)

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $\rho:\mathcal R^\bullet\to\mathcal O'$ ($\mathcal O'$ in degree $0$) from [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. A morphism of complexes is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if its mapping cone is acyclic (long exact cohomology sequence of the cone triangle of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]); so $C^\bullet=\operatorname{Cone}(\alpha)$ and $\operatorname{Cone}(\rho)$ are acyclic. Use the symmetry isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes\mathcal B^\bullet)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal B^\bullet\otimes\mathcal A^\bullet)$, $a\otimes b\mapsto(-1)^{pq}b\otimes a$ on $\mathcal A^p\otimes\mathcal B^q$, of the total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], natural in both arguments. Consider the commutative square with top row $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal R^\bullet\otimes\mathcal P^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal R^\bullet\otimes\mathcal Q^\bullet)$ (induced by $\alpha$), bottom row $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal O'\otimes\mathcal P^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal O'\otimes\mathcal Q^\bullet)$ and vertical maps induced by $\rho$. Top row: by [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] with $\mathcal A^\bullet=\mathcal R^\bullet$ and the morphism $\alpha$, its cone is $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal R^\bullet\otimes C^\bullet)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(C^\bullet\otimes\mathcal R^\bullet)$, acyclic because $C^\bullet$ is acyclic and $\mathcal R^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]; so the top row is a quasi-isomorphism. Left column: after the symmetry it is $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes\mathcal R^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes\mathcal O')$, whose cone is $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes\operatorname{Cone}(\rho))\cong\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Cone}(\rho)\otimes\mathcal P^\bullet)$ by [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso], acyclic because $\operatorname{Cone}(\rho)$ is acyclic and $\mathcal P^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]; likewise the right column with $\mathcal Q^\bullet$. Taking $H^n$ of the commutative square, three of the four maps are isomorphisms, hence so is the bottom row. Since $\mathcal O'$ sits in degree $0$, $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal O'\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal P^\bullet)$ is the complex $\mathcal O'\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal P^n$ with differential $1\otimes d$, identified with $\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ by the symmetry of the tensor product of modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and the bottom row becomes $\alpha\otimes1$. This proves (1).

source.place: Tag 06YT (proof, with F = O' in degree 0)

proof.text: Let $F:K(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$ be $\mathcal G^\bullet\mapsto\mathcal G^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ followed by the localization functor of $D(\mathcal O')$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It is an exact functor of triangulated categories: the termwise functor $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ is additive [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], so it preserves homotopies, commutes with the shift, and carries the cone $C(f)$ (termwise a direct sum with the matrix differential) to the cone $C(f\otimes1)$, and the localization functor is exact. Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Every complex has a quasi-isomorphism from an element of $\mathcal P$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and by Step 1 $F$ sends every quasi-isomorphism between elements of $\mathcal P$ to an isomorphism. Hence [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] applies: the left derived functor $L\varphi^*:=LF:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$ is everywhere defined, is an exact functor of triangulated categories, and comes with its canonical transformation $LF\circ Q\to F$ whose component at every K-flat complex is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 06XN and 05SE, as used in sites-cohomology Tag 06YY

proof.text: For a K-flat resolution $s:\mathcal P^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$, $Q(s)$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O)$, so $LF(Q s)$ is an isomorphism, and the component $LF(Q\mathcal P^\bullet)\to F(\mathcal P^\bullet)=\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ of the canonical transformation is an isomorphism by Step 2. The canonical map $L\varphi^*\mathcal G^\bullet\to\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ is this component composed with $LF(Qs)^{-1}$, an isomorphism. For two resolutions the isomorphism $\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'\cong\mathcal P'^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ is the canonical map for $\mathcal P'^\bullet$ composed with the inverse of the one for $\mathcal P^\bullet$; it depends only on the two resolutions, and for a third resolution $\mathcal P''^\bullet$ the composite of the comparisons $\mathcal P\to\mathcal P'$ and $\mathcal P'\to\mathcal P''$ is the comparison $\mathcal P\to\mathcal P''$ since the middle factors cancel.
